review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/models/tool_class.go:181 (MinimumApprovalFloor), :207 (EffectiveApprovalFloor); apps/Model Plane/rust/crates/mp-contracts/src/tool_class.rs:153 (minimum_floor); capabilities_store.go:152 and :317 (new-row default unclassified/none)
review_defects.scenario: The slice says unknown is strictest, but that holds only for the class. Both twins give `unclassified` the weakest floor, `none`, and every new or unread row defaults to unclassified/none. Under the posture model the slice's own parity test encodes (tool_class_registry_parity.rs declared_posture), floor `none` plus `auto` posture gives Allow. So an unclassified tool that is really an owner effect would run without the durable owner approval a classified owner_effect row must have. Concrete wire result: GET /api/v1/capabilities for any new tenant row, and gRPC GetCapability/ListCapabilities on a store-less capability-core (in-memory registry, where SideEffectClass and ApprovalFloor are ""), report cap.tool.ticket.create as side_effect_class=unclassified, approval_floor=none. A durable-owner capability is advertised with no floor. It also leaves a generic-surface way to lower a floor: soft-delete a row whose floor is ask or durable_owner, then POST the same (org, kind, name) under a new id. enforceClassFloor's prior read filters deleted_at IS NULL, so the recreated row comes back at unclassified/none. The plan's own S3 engine floors unclassified to ask, so the shared contract the gate will read contradicts the plan. Not reachable in S1 for classified tenant rows, because no API path sets a class.
review_defects.fix: Make MinimumApprovalFloor(unclassified) / SideEffectClass::Unclassified.minimum_floor() return `ask`, so EffectiveApprovalFloor reports at least ask for an unclassified row. Add the vector to both known-answer tables. Optionally have enforceClassFloor also compare against the most recent soft-deleted row for the same (org, kind, name).

review_defects.scenario: The Go and Rust twins disagree about an empty floor. Rust ApprovalFloor::from_wire("") is DurableOwner, and Go NormalizeApprovalFloor("") is durable_owner too. But Go EffectiveApprovalFloor, the only function the wire uses (capabilityView, listTools, toDetail), rewrites "" to `none` before raising. Scenario: store-less capability-core, or the in-memory registry fed by capabilities_source.go, which does not scan the new columns. toDetail emits approval_floor="none" for every capability. A pre-S1 server emits "" for proto field 19, and a Rust consumer parses that as DurableOwner. The same row gets the strictest or the weakest floor depending on which server version answered. The known-answer tables do not pin the empty-floor case on the Go side.
review_defects.fix: Have EffectiveApprovalFloor go through NormalizeApprovalFloor ("" -> durable_owner), or treat "" the same way in both twins. Add an empty-floor vector to TestSideEffectClassKnownAnswers and to the Rust known_answers test.

review_defects.scenario: plan.propose is seeded as `read`/`none`, but it writes a plan durably through session-core. Measured, from ChatMessages.render-budget.test.tsx (84 tokens, 19 blocks):
- AnswerRegion mounts 1 (was 84).

- Parse calls 1 per token (was 2).
- Parsed chars 22,357 over the stream, bounded by the last 3 blocks per token. The test asserts the bound and that the total is under the quadratic baseline, but the 22,357 was not run against a baseline here.

What was built:
- parseMarkdownBlocks is now a thin wrapper over parseBlocksFrom(lines, start). Added the exports FROZEN_TAIL_BLOCKS = 2, ParsedMarkdown and parseMarkdownIncremental(prev, source).
- Restart points are recorded per block. A block that starts on the remainder of a comment line the parser rewrote has a null restart point, so a restart steps back to an earlier block.
- A re-read tail block that comes out deep-equal keeps the previous object. This stops the block just before the one being typed from rebuilding its DOM each token (MarkdownList rebuilds its <ul> whenever its block object changes).
- ChatMarkdown keeps a per-instance parse and renders with <For keyed={false}>. ChatMessages keys node rows by nodeKey and renders them through registry.renderLive. The stale comment at the old :653-657 is replaced.
- nodeKey(node) is added in derive.ts, default node.kind.
- ConversationNodeEntry is added in types.ts. renderLive(entry) is added in registry.ts. It passes the unchanged renderers Proxy views backed by one memo per property, so a field that did not change does not notify its readers. It reads the row kind untracked.
- VITE_CHAT_RENDER_LEGACY=true is read through an exact-string check. It restores the old keyed-by-reference rows and the full reparse per token. Tests pin the legacy path and show that "1", "TRUE", "yes" and "" do not enable it.

The paragraph branch re-tested the first line with isMarkdownBlockStart, whose unanchored patterns match while the anchored heading and list patterns do not (because of a trailing "\r" or U+2028). It pushed empty paragraphs without advancing. A stream chunk ending between CR and LF can trigger this. The first line is now taken unconditionally. Output is identical for every input that terminated before, and a regression test is added.
- exportDocument in AssistantMessage now returns null while the turn is streaming. It called answerExportSize, which fully parsed the message on every token; that was the second parse call per token the S1 test had attributed to remounting. showExportButton is already false while streaming and the action row is hidden, so there is no visible change. This applies to the legacy path too, so the legacy pin in the render-budget test is now 1 parse call per token, down from 2.
- The S1 baseline asserts in ChatMessages.render-budget.test.tsx are flipped to the S2 targets. Sealed is now defined as "already followed by another block at the previous token". The parse measure for parseMarkdownIncremental is the text from its resume line. The file is still CRLF.
- nodeKey is imported from '@/shared/chat-nodes/derive' because the barrel is not owned.
- The new test files are LF; registry.ts and the render-budget test stay CRLF.

notes:
DONE
- BrowserObservation.challenge: Option<BrowserChallenge> with closed enums ChallengeKind, ChallengeStrength, BlockReason, ChallengeRecovery, confidence_per_mille. Every construction site now has challenge: None. Display renders typed fields only.
- quarry_agent: WireObservation.challenge uses a lenient deserializer. An older Quarry without the field parses, a legacy signal with no strength reads as strong, and a malformed challenge is dropped without failing the observation. Unknown vocabulary values degrade: kind to Unknown, strength to Weak (a hint, never a verdict), block_reason to None, recovery to NotApplicable. Evidence strings are never read, since they are page text.
- llm_planner: BROWSER_CHALLENGE_RULE is appended to the planner system prompt. observation_text adds a "challenge:" line for strong and weak signals only. non_signal (login, consent, paywall, rate limit) and no signal give no line, so the prompt is byte-identical to before in those cases.
- model-gateway: the same text is a const BROWSER_CHALLENGE_RULE, used through browser_suggest_system_prompt() in browser_suggest_action.
- tests/browser_challenge_rule_contract.rs reads both sources. It checks the texts are equal, that anchor phrases are kept, that each constant is actually sent in its prompt, and that CRLF is not drift. It is mutation-tested (loosened budget on either side, a sentence lost on both, constant renamed or commented out, use removed).
- DECISION TAKEN: a 403 with error.code CHALLENGE_DETECTED on a browser step maps to AgentClientError::Challenge, and the loop turns it into an ObservationStatus::Blocked observation carrying challenge{strong, block_reason, exhausted}. plan_next_action already stops on any Blocked observation ("action blocked: ..."), so the run ends blocked with no retry. Any other 403 (FORBIDDEN, SECURITY_BLOCKED, USER_TOOK_OVER) and any other status stay AgentClientError::Status. block_reason is read from details.block_reason, then details.reason. Reason: a refused wall is Quarry's final verdict (retryable:false), and a Status error is what the loop and the MCP path treat as a generic failure. Tested through the real loop with wiremock (the step mock has expect(1), so there is no retry).
- Addition beyond the brief: the planner schema has no "blocked" action, so the rule says to report blocked as action=done. blocked_by_bot_wall() makes a planner "done" over a page whose last observation is still strong fail the run ("blocked: the site refuses automation (...)") instead of completing it. Weak, non_signal and no signal still complete normally.

DEVIATIONS
- The brief says "ONE wait ... and ONE reload". Quarry grants one recovery per host and run, either a wait or a reload, and refuses the second. The rule therefore says ONE recovery step: a single wait of up to 5 seconds, or a single reload of the same page.
- The refusal observation carries confidence_per_mille 1000 and kind Unknown, since the refusal body has neither.
- The rule text is a single-line raw string (r"...") so the contract test is independent of line endings.

CAVEATS
- The gateway browser_suggest_action planner is handed the whole Quarry observation JSON by its caller. That is pre-existing, but with WS3.J it can now include challenge.evidence strings, which are page-derived. Only the execution-core planner has the typed-fields-only guarantee. Consider stripping evidence in the gateway or the SPA, in a later slice.
- The MCP path (execution_quarry_browser_mcp) serializes WireObservation, so it now also carries the typed challenge fields when Quarry sends them (typed only, no evidence). A refused MCP step returns the error text "bot challenge (kind=... block_reason=...)".
- Pre-existing clippy warnings in these files are untouched.
